sentences.text: Brasileodactylus was a medium-sized flying reptile with a wingspan reaching about four meters.
Its head featured an elongated, sharp beak and narrow, cone-shaped teeth located at the front of the jaws.
This species differed from other Brazilian relatives by the absence of a ridge on its snout or lower jaw, although a crest on the back of the skull remains possible.
A 2026 study describes a lower jaw of Brasileodactylus araripensis from the Romualdo Formation that provides evidence of a mandibular crest.
Fossils of this animal were recovered from the lower Santana Formation within the Aptian stage in the Chapada do Araripe region of Ceará, Brazil.
The genus name Brasileodactylus was established by paleontologist Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner in 1984.
The defining specimen, cataloged as MN 4804-V, preserves only the anterior portion of a jaw.
Brasileodactylus belongs to the broader group known as Ornithocheiroidea.
It is classified within the class Reptilia.

Taxonomic opinions have shifted over time; Kellner moved it from Ornithocheiridae to uncertain Pterodactyloidea, then suggested a link to Anhangueridae, while others proposed connections to Anhanguera, Coloborhynchus, or even treated Ludodactylus as a synonym.
